pr_title: Bluetooth: Mesh: Fix lpn groups add when node reset
pr_body:
Add lpn groups when model sub restore after reset.

Add auto sub `ALL_NODE_ADDR` when provisioned.

Remove all groups when node unprovisoned.

Fixes: #24311
Fixes: #24009

Signed-off-by: Lingao Meng <mengabc1086@gmail.com>
pr_comments:
**All checks are passing now.**

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Mesh: Friend node not cache ALL_Node Address or different app_idx
issue_context.body:
Set up there nodes, call publish node, friend node ,lpn node.

All node share single network key, but friend & lpn node with different application key, 
the lpn node has same application key will publish node.

when publish node periodic send model message with the dst = 0xffff, lpn node not receive all of them.
comments:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/c98652b42f12f07736259788ba067d8987387cb9/subsys/bluetooth/mesh/transport.c#L905-L914 and sdu_recv_seg

should be change as return 0 ?

I remember seeing some discussion in the Mesh WG about this, with the conclusion that LPNs need to explicitly subscribe to these addresses, so based on that it's not a bug. @trond-snekvik can you confirm?

I remember this too, according to spec, the LPN has to explicitly subscribe to 0xffff. There's no public API for doing this in zephyr though, as it's controlled by the config server, which won't accept 0xffff. Perhaps it could be compile time option to automatically subscribe to 0xffff when the friendship is established?

well, it's still another problem, friend node has different `appkey `with lpn node , but currently call `sud_recv` return `-EINVAL` when local node unable find `appkey`,
so, even the friend node known its dst is lpn node,  and not store this to friend queue.
@LingaoMeng let's not mix multiple issues into a single GitHub issue. Open a new one since I already categorised this based on the 0xffff address concern.

review_comments: IMO, this functionality should be compile time configurable. The working group made it opt-in for a reason, it's very easy to flood the friend queue with broadcast packets that might not be relevant for the LPN
Agreed, and I'd default to disabled for the new option (not just because it seems to be the safe choice but also to keep consistency with previous Zephyr versions).

An alternative would be to expose the group add/del functions as public API (and clearly document that they should only be used for special cases like this, whereas the stack takes automatically care of the rest). Thoughts?
Answering to myself: I'm mildly leaning toward the Kconfig since then the app can't mess around with what the stack manages automatically (e.g. remove groups that the stack had added, etc).
